title: Exterior products commute with the compact-support projection transformation
statement:
Use the finite-field datum and finite coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ and the actual operations of [sk-def-sf-operations], on separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Let $f_i:X_i\to Y_i$ be separated finite-type morphisms, $M_i\in D^b_{ctf}(X_i,A)$ and $B_i\in D^b_{ctf}(Y_i,A)$, for $i=1,2$. Put $f=f_1\times f_2$, $M=M_1\boxtimes M_2$, $B=B_1\boxtimes B_2$ and $C_i=M_i\otimes^LLf_i^*B_i$. Let $\operatorname{PF}_{f,M,B}:Rf_!M\otimes^LB\to Rf_!(M\otimes^LLf^*B)$ be the specified projection transformation [def-exchange-projection]. Let $K_M:Rf_!(M_1\boxtimes M_2)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{1!}M_1\boxtimes Rf_{2!}M_2$ and $K_C:Rf_!(C_1\boxtimes C_2)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{1!}C_1\boxtimes Rf_{2!}C_2$ be precisely the maps $\mathrm{Ku}_!$ of [sk-def-sf-kv-maps](i). Let $\delta:M\otimes^LLf^*B\xrightarrow{\sim}C_1\boxtimes C_2$ be the canonical pullback-composition, monoidal pullback and signed tensor interchange, and let $\xi:(Rf_{1!}M_1\boxtimes Rf_{2!}M_2)\otimes^LB\xrightarrow{\sim}(Rf_{1!}M_1\otimes^LB_1)\boxtimes(Rf_{2!}M_2\otimes^LB_2)$ be signed tensor interchange on the targets. Then the following equality of specified natural morphisms holds:
$$K_C\circ Rf_!(\delta)\circ\operatorname{PF}_{f,M,B}=(\operatorname{PF}_{f_1,M_1,B_1}\boxtimes\operatorname{PF}_{f_2,M_2,B_2})\circ\xi\circ(K_M\otimes1_B).$$
All tensors are derived over the constant sheaf $A$. No exceptional inverse image or external internal-Hom comparison occurs in this assertion.

source.place: Beta, last sentence, projection-formula compatibility needed before applying the exceptional counits; the canonical Ku_! is the relative product composite of sk-thm-sf-kunneth-relative.

proof.text: Work with the actual finite coefficients \(A=A_{E,n}\) and operations of [sk-def-sf-operations]. Put \(F_i=Rf_{i!}M_i\), \(H=F_1\boxtimes F_2\), and \(D=C_1\boxtimes C_2\). Pullback, tensor and compact support preserve the finite-Tor constructible domains by [thm-sf-ctf-stability](i),(ii),(iv), including extension by zero for open immersions. All these objects are of bounded etale origin by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii). Thus the witnessed compactification comparisons used below apply. We always use the monoidal pullback comparisons of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], including their signed symmetry and composition coherence, and the projection maps of [def-exchange-projection]. These give the stated \(\delta\) and \(\xi\) with exactly the displayed sources and targets.

source.place: The map beta, final paragraph: projection compatibility before the two evaluation maps.

proof.text:
First suppose \(f_i\) proper. Write \(s_i:Y_1\times Y_2\to Y_i\), \(h_1=f_1\times1\), \(h_2=1\times f_2\), and \(r_i:\operatorname{dom}(h_i)\to X_i\). Set \(Q_i=Lr_i^*M_i\). The base-change isomorphisms built into [sk-def-sf-kv-maps](i) are
\[b_i:Ls_i^*F_i\longrightarrow Rh_{i*}Q_i.\]
They are the proper exchanges of [def-exchange-projection]. Let \(\lambda_h\) be the forward relative composite displayed in [lem-sf-proper-product-counit-transpose], for \((h_1,h_2;Q_1,Q_2)\). Reversing the arrows in the definition of [sk-thm-sf-kunneth-relative] gives, with the canonical product pullback identifications,
\[L_M:=K_M^{-1}=\lambda_h\circ(b_1\otimes b_2):H\longrightarrow Rf_*M.\]
In particular \(K_M^{-1}\) is not identified with \(\lambda_h\) before these exchanges are inserted. Define \(L_C=K_C^{-1}\) by exactly the same formula with \(M_i\) replaced by \(C_i\).

source.place: The map beta, final paragraph: projection compatibility before the two evaluation maps.

proof.text:
For each \(i\), the exchange mate formula in [def-exchange-projection] gives
\[\varepsilon_{h_i,Q_i}\circ Lh_i^*b_i
 =Lr_i^*\varepsilon_{f_i,M_i}\circ\theta_i,\]
where \(\theta_i:Lh_i^*Ls_i^*\cong Lr_i^*Lf_i^*\). Apply the second transpose formula of [lem-sf-proper-product-counit-transpose] to \(\lambda_h\), then precompose with \(Lf^*(b_1\otimes b_2)\). The two factors in its transpose are precisely the two left sides of this equation, pulled back from \(\operatorname{dom}(h_i)\) to \(X_1\times X_2\). Substitution yields
\[\varepsilon_{f,M}\circ Lf^*L_M=c_M,
\qquad c_M:=\varepsilon_{f_1,M_1}\boxtimes\varepsilon_{f_2,M_2}:Lf^*H\to M.\]
Here \(\boxtimes\) on maps includes the canonical pullback and tensor comparisons. Since \(L_MK_M=1\), this also proves the previously missing identity
\[\varepsilon_{f,M}=c_M\circ Lf^*K_M.\]
Replacing \(M_i\) by \(C_i\) gives \(\varepsilon_{f,D}\circ Lf^*L_C=c_C\). The ordinary adjunction and its composite normalization are [fix-prop-adjunctions](1),(3); no exceptional counit is involved.

source.place: The map beta, final paragraph: projection compatibility before the two evaluation maps.

proof.text:
Put \(P_i=\operatorname{PF}_{f_i,M_i,B_i}\). For proper maps use the trivial compactification \((\mathrm{id},f_i)\): its open projection isomorphism \(\gamma\) is the identity by [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] with \(j=\mathrm{id}\), so \(P_i=\pi_{f_i;M_i,B_i}\), and likewise for \(f\). Compare the two maps to the SAME object \(Rf_*D\):
\[u=Rf_*(\delta)\operatorname{PF}_{f,M,B},\qquad
v=L_C(P_1\boxtimes P_2)\xi(K_M\otimes1).\]
Their ordinary transposes have domain \(Lf^*(Rf_*M\otimes B)\). By [def-exchange-projection] the transpose of \(u\) is \(\delta(\varepsilon_{f,M}\otimes1)\mu_f\). By step 3 the transpose of \(v\) is \(c_C Lf^*((P_1\boxtimes P_2)\xi(K_M\otimes1))\). For each factor the counit projection definition says
\[\varepsilon_{f_i,C_i}Lf_i^*P_i
 =(\varepsilon_{f_i,M_i}\otimes1)\mu_{f_i}.\]
This is also the FIRST formula of [lem-sf-proper-product-counit-transpose] with its \(f=f_i\), \(g=\mathrm{id}_{Y_i}\), \(K=M_i\), \(L=B_i\), hence \(q=f_i\) and the exchange is identity. Consequently both transposes are the following typed composite:
\[Lf^*(Rf_*M\otimes B)\xrightarrow{Lf^*(K_M\otimes1)}Lf^*(H\otimes B)
 \cong (Lf_1^*F_1\otimes Lf_1^*B_1)\boxtimes(Lf_2^*F_2\otimes Lf_2^*B_2)
 \xrightarrow{(\varepsilon_{f_1,M_1}\otimes1)\boxtimes(\varepsilon_{f_2,M_2}\otimes1)}D.\]
The middle comparison is the signed one: its equality in the two expansions follows from the symmetry and composition clauses of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. Injectivity of the ordinary Hom bijection [fix-prop-adjunctions](1) gives \(u=v\); composing with \(K_C\) proves the proper case.

source.place: The map beta, final paragraph: projection compatibility before the two evaluation maps.

proof.text:
For the general case choose \(f_i=a_i j_i\), with \(j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow\bar X_i\) open and \(a_i\) proper. Such compactifications exist by [thm-nagata-compactification]: the targets are quasi-compact and quasi-separated since they are separated and finite type over a field. Use \(f=aj\), \(a=a_1\times a_2\), \(j=j_1\times j_2\). Put
\[N_i=j_{i!}M_i,\quad A_i=La_i^*B_i,\quad V_i=N_i\otimes A_i,\quad T_i=j_{i!}C_i,\quad N=N_1\boxtimes N_2,\quad T=T_1\boxtimes T_2.\]
Write \(\gamma_i:V_i\to T_i\) and \(\gamma_j:j_!M\otimes La^*B\to j_!(M\otimes Lf^*B)\) for the open projection isomorphisms of [def-exchange-projection]. Let
\[e_M:N\to j_!M,\quad e_C:T\to j_!D\]
be the normalized comparisons of [lem-sf-open-external-tensor-normalization], and let \(\bar\delta:N\otimes La^*B\to V_1\boxtimes V_2\) be signed interchange. The domain assertions of step 1 apply also on the compactifications (which are separated finite type) and to all these objects.

source.place: The map beta, final paragraph: projection compatibility before the two evaluation maps.

proof.text:
The required open coefficient square, on \(j_!M\otimes La^*B\), is
\[e_C^{-1}\,j_!(\delta)\,\gamma_j
 =(\gamma_1\boxtimes\gamma_2)\,\bar\delta\,(e_M^{-1}\otimes1).\tag{O}\]
Here is its proof, rather than an appeal to base-change pasting. Precompose both sides with \(\gamma_j^{-1}\); they are now maps FROM \(j_!(M\otimes Lf^*B)\). Under the open adjunction it suffices to compare their restrictions, since the unit \(1\to j^*j_!\) is an isomorphism [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. The restrictions of \(e_M,e_C\) are identities by [lem-sf-open-external-tensor-normalization], and those of every \(\gamma\) are identities by [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Finally \(j^*\bar\delta=\delta\) by monoidal pullback composition [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. Thus both restricted maps are exactly \(\delta\), proving (O). This is a direct open-adjunction calculation; no displayed hypothesis of lem-sf-pf-compactification-pasting is used as a theorem.

source.place: The map beta, final paragraph: projection compatibility before the two evaluation maps.

proof.text:
Write \(K^a_N,K^a_T\) for the exterior Kunneth maps of \((a_1,a_2)\). Under \(Rf_{i!}=Ra_{i*}j_{i!}\), the product compactification identity gives
\[K_M=K^a_N\,Ra_*(e_M^{-1}),\qquad K_C=K^a_T\,Ra_*(e_C^{-1}).\tag{K}\]
To specify the exchanges in this application, apply [lem-sf-product-compactification-identity] to \(h_i\) of step 2, compactified by \(\bar h_1=a_1\times1\), \(\bar h_2=1\times a_2\) and their opens \(v_i\). Open base change identifies \(v_{i!}Lr_i^*M_i\) with \(L\bar r_i^*j_{i!}M_i\). In the notation \(b_i\) of step 2, [def-exchange-projection]'s compactification formula is explicitly
\[b_i^f=R\bar h_{i*}(\beta_i)\,b_i^a,\quad
\beta_i:L\bar r_i^*j_{i!}M_i\to v_{i!}Lr_i^*M_i.\]
Naturality of the relative forward composite in its two inputs [sk-thm-sf-kunneth-relative] moves these \(\beta_i\) through \(\lambda_{\bar h_1,\bar h_2}\). The product compactification identity then reads
\[K_M^{-1}=Ra_*(e_M)(K^a_N)^{-1}.\]
Indeed put \(e'=e_{v_1,v_2}\circ(\beta_1\boxtimes\beta_2)\), its source identified with that of \(e_M\) by pullback composition. Each \(\beta_i\) restricts to the identity on the open [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], and \(e_{v_1,v_2}\), \(e_M\) restrict to the identity [lem-sf-open-external-tensor-normalization]. So \(e'e_M^{-1}\) is an endomorphism of \(j_!M\) restricting to the identity; full faithfulness of \(j_!\) [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] gives \(e'=e_M\). Inverting gives (K); replacing \(M_i\) by \(C_i\) gives the second formula. This uses the exact relative definition of [sk-def-sf-kv-maps](i), including its two exchanges.

source.place: The map beta, final paragraph: projection compatibility before the two evaluation maps.

proof.text:
Let \(\Gamma=\gamma_1\boxtimes\gamma_2\), \(P_a=\operatorname{PF}_{a,N,B}\), and \(P_{a_i}=\operatorname{PF}_{a_i,N_i,B_i}\). The proper case already proved, applied to \((a_i,N_i,B_i)\), says
\[K^a_{V_1,V_2}\,Ra_*(\bar\delta)P_a
 =(P_{a_1}\boxtimes P_{a_2})\xi(K^a_N\otimes1).\]
Naturality in the two coefficient complexes in [sk-thm-sf-kunneth-relative], with [sk-def-sf-kv-maps](i), gives
\[K^a_T Ra_*(\Gamma)
 =(Ra_{1*}\gamma_1\boxtimes Ra_{2*}\gamma_2)K^a_{V_1,V_2}.\]
Multiply the first equality by the displayed coefficient maps and use the defining formula \(\operatorname{PF}_{f_i}=Ra_{i*}(\gamma_i)P_{a_i}\) from [def-exchange-projection]. This yields the explicit equality
\[K^a_T Ra_*(\Gamma\bar\delta)P_a
 =(\operatorname{PF}_{f_1}\boxtimes\operatorname{PF}_{f_2})\xi(K^a_N\otimes1).\tag{P}\]
Every projection map here has second variable \(B_i\), or \(B=B_1\boxtimes B_2\); no base-change projection square is substituted for this naturality square.

source.place: The map beta, final paragraph: projection compatibility before the two evaluation maps.

proof.text:
Set \(q=Ra_*(e_M^{-1}):Rf_!M\to Ra_*N\), and let \(P'_a=\pi_{a;j_!M,B}\). Ordinary projection naturality [def-exchange-projection] says
\[Ra_*(e_M^{-1}\otimes1)P'_a=P_a(q\otimes1).\]
Now compute the left-hand side of the asserted equality using (K), the compactification formula for \(\operatorname{PF}_f\), (O), this naturality, and (P), in that order:
\[\begin{aligned}
K_C Rf_!(\delta)\operatorname{PF}_f
 &=K^a_T Ra_*(e_C^{-1}j_!(\delta)\gamma_j)P'_a\\
 &=K^a_T Ra_*(\Gamma\bar\delta)Ra_*(e_M^{-1}\otimes1)P'_a\\
 &=K^a_T Ra_*(\Gamma\bar\delta)P_a(q\otimes1)\\
 &=(\operatorname{PF}_{f_1}\boxtimes\operatorname{PF}_{f_2})\xi(K^a_N\otimes1)(q\otimes1)\\
 &=(\operatorname{PF}_{f_1}\boxtimes\operatorname{PF}_{f_2})\xi(K_M\otimes1).
\end{aligned}\]
All five lines start at \(Rf_!M\otimes B\) and end at \(Rf_{1!}C_1\boxtimes Rf_{2!}C_2\). This is the required equality at the product compactification.

source.place: The map beta, final paragraph: projection compatibility before the two evaluation maps.

proof.text: Finally, [lem-fix-projection-compactification-comparison] identifies the chosen-compactification projection maps with the specified ones on the bounded etale-origin domain checked in step 1: its equation is \(\rho(C)\operatorname{PF}^{c}=\operatorname{PF}^{c'}(\rho(M)\otimes1)\). The exchanges \(b_i\) of step 2, hence their compactification formula in step 7, are independent of the compactification and commute with refinement comparisons [fix-lem-exchanges](4). The product identity used in (K) is compatible with the same refinement comparisons [lem-sf-product-compactification-identity]; hence the calculation holds for the specified \(K_M,K_C\), not just for one presentation. The coefficient naturality used in step 8 is expressly part of [sk-thm-sf-kunneth-relative]. This proves the stated formula with its original \(\delta,\xi\) and coefficients, without any exceptional inverse image or external internal-Hom map.

split_report.summary: Repairs both returned compatibility gaps without changing the statement. Inserts the two base-change exchanges in the proper inverse Kunneth map and derives their counit-mate identities, then compares correctly typed ordinary transposes, with the first proper transpose formula explicitly specialized to g=id. Proves the open external/projection coefficient square directly by open adjunction and identity restrictions, and replaces the unsupported pasting invocation and conjugation claim by displayed naturality equations and a five-line composite calculation. Adds the relative Kunneth coefficient-naturality citation and checks bounded etale-origin and finite-Tor domains. No new nodes: the open square is an elementary restriction calculation from existing normalization statements.
